answer.generated: Two primary design issues in distributed systems engineering are transparency and openness. Transparency concerns the extent to which a distributed system should appear to the user as a single entity, balancing the need for simplicity in user experience with the reality of system complexity. Openness involves deciding whether to design the system using standard protocols that promote interoperability or more specialized protocols that offer greater control but potentially limit flexibility and compatibility with other systems.
